newsitem.title: INDIA: Two unexploded bombs found near India train track.
newsitem.headline: Two unexploded bombs found near India train track.

text.p: Two unexploded bombs were found along a railway track in northern India less than 24 hours after an explosion shattered a sleeper carriage in a train and killed 12 people, police said on Wednesday.
They said the bombs were found by a man on a motor scooter late on Monday near Samba town, 40 km (25 miles) southeast of Jammu city, the winter capital of Jammu and Kashmir state.
The devices were wrapped in a bag and placed beside the railway track.

Earlier on Monday, a powerful blast ripped through a train in Ambala cantonment station, about 250 km (150 miles) southeast of Samba, killing 12 and injuring 37. The train was destined for Samba and Jammu.
No one has claimed responsibility for the Ambala blast, which stirred fears of a resurgence of violence in Punjab state.
For a decade until the early 1990s, the fertile region bordering Pakistan was racked by a separatist rebellion in which more than 20,000 people were killed.
Investigators said on Tuesday that they believed Kashmiri, not Sikh, militants had planted the bomb.
A senior police official in the capital of Punjab state, Chandigarh, said Kashmiri militants rarely claim responsibility for bomb attacks, while Sikh guerrillas do.
But Home (Interior) Minister Indrajit Gupta was quoted on Wednesday as saying there were indications that the Sikh separatist group Babbar Khalsa may have been behind the blast.

Punjab police chief Sube Singh told Reuters that the explosives used in the train attack sparked a raging fire like the one that followed the assassination of Punjab chief minister Beant Singh in 1995.
Babbar Khalsa claimed responsibility for Singh's murder.
Satyendra Kumar, deputy police chief of Haryana state, which borders Punjab, said the blast could have been a coordinated effort between Sikh and Kashmiri militants.
"We suspect it could be a combined effort between Sikh militants and Kashmiri militants as both are experts in explosives," Kumar told Reuters in Chandigarh.
Dozens of separatist groups are fighting Indian rule in Jammu and Kashmir, mostly Hindu India's only Moslem majority state, which neighbours Punjab to the north.
